$description: Shadows/elevation for the 'adminlte-classic' template (Classic Admin). Obtained by observing the public visual identity of AdminLTE — discreet, two-layer shadows (an almost imperceptible outline plus a soft diffusion), never heavy/dramatic shadows. Original document — see ATTRIBUTION.md.

card.$description: Default elevation for cards and panels: an almost imperceptible 1px outline (12.5% opacity) combined with a soft 3px diffusion (20% opacity). The effect is subtle, not dramatic.

raised.$description: Elevation for floating elements: dropdowns, popovers, table row action menus.

dark.$description: Dark-theme counterparts, mirroring shadow.card and shadow.raised the way tokens/colors-dark.json mirrors the palette. A shadow is a darkening, and darkening a near-black surface does almost nothing — so in this theme elevation is carried mainly by the step between color.dark.surface.muted and color.dark.surface.canvas, with these shadows only reinforcing it. See foundations/theming.md. shadow.none needs no counterpart: it is the same absence in either theme.

card.$description: Default card elevation. Same geometry as shadow.card, built from black at a much higher opacity — the light theme's rgba(33, 37, 41, 0.125) is very nearly the colour of the dark page itself and would be invisible. Even at these opacities it reads as a faint seam rather than a lift, which is expected: on this theme the surface step does the work.

raised.$description: Floating elements: dropdown panels, tooltips, row action menus. This is the one case where a dark-theme shadow still earns its place — a floating panel shares its background with the surface it covers, so without a shadow its edge is the only thing separating them. Pair it with a 1px color.dark.surface.border, which the light theme could get away with treating as optional.
